title: The Five Garments of the First Man and the Pentecost of the Soul
arc: From the cosmic descent of the First Man clothed in five garments and the joining of the Call with the Answer, the teaching unfolds the conveyance of the Living Soul upward — and shows how that primordial event becomes present in the fifty holy days of fasting, the living food by which the soul is filled with power, riches, life, and light until the coming of Jesus the Radiance.
reading:
This chapter takes a single thread and follows it from the highest cosmic event down to the ordered life of the elect on earth. It begins with the five garments in which the First Man — Divine Truth descending into the realm of self-love — clothed himself for his mission, and it ends with the fifty holy days in which the soul, eating its "living food," is conveyed upward by the same power that originally carried the First Man home.

The opening establishes the structure. The First Man wears five garments, and within each garment there are five powers. The five garments are the Five Sons of the First Man, the elements as Living Soul, the five attributes of Divine Truth in its descent. The five inner powers are the five faculties of reception (mind, thought, teaching, counsel, reflection) folded within each. Read correspondentially, the teaching is showing how Divine Truth, when it accommodates itself to the natural, must take on the complete five-fold structure of the natural-rational interface — and how at every level of that structure it carries the same five-fold receptivity within itself. The garments are external truths clothing the inmost; the powers are the receptive faculties answering to those truths from within. They are "reckoned to one another" because each outer garment corresponds with an inner power; correspondence is the pairing.

The middle of the teaching is the great cosmogonic event that sets the whole arc in motion: "The Call went downward; the Answer rose upward to come up with him." This is the redemptive heart of the chapter. The Call is the influx of Divine Truth reaching downward to the captive Living Soul; the Answer is the soul's receptive return — the Hearing that meets the summons. When they join, what is produced is described as "twenty characters in twenty members." Read through correspondence, this is the perfected articulation of the regenerate human: four times five, the ordered fullness in extension applied to the complete structure of the natural-rational, written into the very members of the redeemed. These joined characters-in-members are then named "the children of mankind" — not the proprium-human Adam, but the human as remade through the conjoining of Call and Answer.

It is by this joining that the Living Soul is carried home. The Call and Answer together "convey them upward to the Height by their hand" — they function as the hand of ascent, the very mechanism by which the Living Man (the First Man as the soul's archetype) is raised. By this same operation the children of light are raised "away from all the works of darkness and (those) below." The vertical motion of redemption belongs not to the soul alone nor to the Lord alone, but to the conjunction of summons and response.

From this height the teaching descends to its liturgical application. The days on which this conjunction is enacted in the church are called Pentecost — "the Fifty of the great days." The number is precise: five faculties multiplied by the ten-fold broader completeness yields the full sabbatical extension of the redemptive event. These are holy days of fasting, days in which the soul abstains from the food of the proprium so that it may eat instead the "living food" which is itself the Call and the Answer. From that time onward, the teaching says, until the coming of Jesus the Radiance the Glorious One, this living food has been the sustenance by which the elect are spiritually released from the houses of bondage. The fifty days suffice for them all; the food fills them with power, with riches, with life, with light — the four-fold inner abundance that flows from conjunction.

Then the fifty becomes a hundred. The completed cycle of Call-and-Answer reduplicates itself: a hundred holy days, the doubled fullness, marking the second descent that answers the first. Where the surviving text breaks down toward the end, two pairings stand visible and govern the closing: the mysteries of the first aeons over against the second ones, and the First Man over against the Second Man. The teaching closes by linking the original cosmic event to its repetition in Christ. The First Man's descent in five garments and the joining of his Call with his Answer is the archetype; Jesus the Radiance, the Second Man, comes as the same event made manifest in the world, and the fifty-day fast is the way the church in time enters that one perpetual rising.

Read as a whole, the chapter teaches that regeneration is not a private movement of the soul but the lived participation in a cosmic correspondence: every garment of truth has its inward power; every Call from above has its Answer from below; every fifty has its hundred; every First Man has his Second. The fast is not deprivation but the soul's eating of the Call-and-Answer themselves, by which the twenty characters are written into the twenty members and the human is conveyed upward by that very hand.
